1.why: /api/verify only looks up the token in the recoveries map and binds record.flowId to the verifying session; no email or user identity is ever associated with a token, so no ownership check exists.

2.why: Tokens are bearer credentials — any session presenting a valid, unused token passes verification (only used/expiry/block flags are checked), though single-use (record.used = true) prevents replay after consumption.

3.why: A password reset only replaces the global passwordHash and sets resetComplete on the current session; there is no logic invalidating other existing sessions.

4.why: The app serves via Bun.serve TLS with a cert/key, redirects all HTTP to HTTPS with a 308, and sets HSTS with preload, but the TLS version is not pinned (defaults negotiate up to TLS 1.3).

5.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed and tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues, but reset tokens are stored in cleartext in the in-memory recoveries map rather than hashed or encrypted.

6.why: The simulated message is returned only to the requesting session over HTTPS, but the reset token is then written into the visible on-page Logs panel and browser console.

7.why: Server-side validation enforces strict length caps, a conservative email regex, token format regex, and typed checks with a bounded JSON parser, and the client renders all data via textContent only.

8.why: The only redirect in the system is the HTTP listener's fixed Location to https://localhost:PORT, the client uses hash-based routing, and no external URLs exist anywhere.

9.why: The mock delivery message is a fixed server-side string rendered via textContent, and no user-supplied input is ever embedded in any message or template.

10.why: Server error responses are generic, but the client explicitly logs the reset token and MFA code to the visible Logs panel and console, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are retained only as Argon2id hashes, but the MFA secret "482916" and the "initial-placeholder-value" password are hardcoded directly in the source.

12.why: The hardcoded MFA code 482916 and the initial placeholder password effectively function as default/fixed credentials, so the statement does not hold.

13.why: Verification is limited to 5 attempts per IP per 10-minute window with a 10-minute block, recovery requests are capped per IP and per session, and 5 MFA failures clear the flow.

14.why: /api/recovery returns the identical generic message ("If an account can be recovered...") for any well-formed email, revealing nothing about account existence.

15.why: The token is 32 CSPRNG bytes (64 hex chars) with a 15-minute expiry — random and complex — but it is not bound to any user or email, so it is not user-specific.
